articles.title: Redemoinho de poeira se forma às margens de estrada e surpreende em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo a Defesa Civil, condições de calor, baixa umidade e solo seco favorecem a formação do fenômeno.
articles.summary: Segundo a Defesa Civil, condições de calor, baixa umidade e solo seco favorecem a formação do fenômeno.
articles.body:
Uma imagem que circula nas redes sociais mostra um redemoinho de poeira de grande proporção na região do Urucum, em Corumbá (MS). O fenômeno aparece próximo a uma estrada, enquanto caminhões e outros veículos passam pela via. Veja o vídeo acima.

Apesar do susto, não houve registro de estragos ou danos causados pelo fenômeno.

Segundo o superintendente da Defesa Civil de Corumbá, capitão-bombeiro Silvanei Coelho, esse tipo de fenômeno é relativamente comum na região, principalmente no trecho entre o assentamento São Gabriel e Albuquerque.

"A Defesa Civil já atendeu situações de maior intensidade nessa região, com redemoinhos capazes de provocar danos materiais e até atingir residências", afirma.

Ainda segundo o superintendente, o calor extremo, a baixa umidade do ar, o solo seco e aquecido e a instabilidade térmica próxima à superfície favorecem a formação desses redemoinhos.

"O redemoinho ocorre quando o ar muito quente, junto ao solo, sobe rapidamente e, encontrando condições favoráveis de circulação de vento, passa a girar, formando essa coluna de poeira característica", explica.

Apesar de, em geral, terem curta duração, alguns redemoinhos podem ganhar intensidade e causar danos.

A orientação da Defesa Civil é manter distância e procurar um local seguro ao perceber a aproximação do fenômeno.

articles.title: Has Gaza broken the Israel consensus in the US?
articles.summary: For decades, Israel was untouchable in Washington. Gaza changed that. Josh Rushing investigates how and what comes next.
articles.body:
For decades, US support for Israel was one of Washington’s few unbreakable bipartisan positions. The genocide in Gaza has changed that.

Josh Rushing is joined by Matt Duss, former policy adviser to US Senator Bernie Sanders, and Kelley Vlahos, editor-in-chief of Responsible Statecraft, to examine how a war that killed more than 74,000 Palestinians fractured Democratic and Republican coalitions alike – reshaping primaries, campus politics and the terms on which a generation now sees Israel and American power.

articles.title: Incêndios em Juruti e Monte Alegre mobilizam equipes no Pará | G1
articles.standfirst: Baixa umidade, altas temperaturas e vegetação seca aumentam o risco de queimadas no oeste do Pará.
articles.summary: Incêndios em Juruti e Monte Alegre mobilizam bombeiros e brigadistas devido à estiagem e baixa umidade que atingem o oeste do Pará.
articles.body:
Incêndios mobilizam equipes de segurança em Juruti e Monte Alegre — Foto: Divulgação/Ascom Alcoa

O período de estiagem tem aumentado o risco de incêndios florestais no oeste do Pará. Em Juruti e Monte Alegre , equipes de segurança e combate a incêndios estão mobilizadas para controlar as chamas e evitar que o fogo avance para outras áreas.

Em Juruti, o combate às queimadas conta com a atuação integrada da Defesa Civil, Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente (SEMMA), Corpo de Bombeiros e brigadistas. A estrutura também recebe oio de equipes de uma mineradora que atua no município.

Segundo a empresa, são 33 bombeiros civis e 117 brigadistas preparados para atuar durante o período mais crítico da estiagem. As equipes também utilizam drones e monitoramento para identificar possíveis focos de incêndio.

A atuação ocorre tanto em áreas operacionais quanto em pontos da cidade e da zona rural. A orientação dos órgãos responsáveis é para que moradores evitem o uso do fogo para limpeza de terrenos, roçados e áreas agrícolas, principalmente neste período de vegetação seca e baixa umidade.

Baixa umidade, altas temperaturas e vegetação seca aumentam o risco de queimadas no oeste do Pará — Foto: Divulgação/Ascom Alcoa

Também é recomendado evitar fogos de artifício próximos a áreas de mata e não descartar cigarros acesos às margens de estradas e rodovias. Garrafas e outros objetos de vidro não devem ser deixados em áreas de vegetação, devido ao risco de provocar incêndios.

Em Monte Alegre, cinco militares do Corpo de Bombeiros estão mobilizados desde o dia 26 de setembro no combate a um incêndio na região do KM 35, setor 14.

As equipes trabalham para controlar as chamas e impedir que o fogo avance para outras áreas. Após a atuação nesse ponto, os militares devem seguir para uma área da CANP, também em Monte Alegre, onde há registro de outro incêndio.

A situação exige atenção por causa das condições climáticas registradas na região, com período de estiagem, temperaturas elevadas e vegetação mais seca, fatores que favorecem a propagação das chamas.

O Corpo de Bombeiros orienta que, em caso de incêndio, a população não tente combater o fogo por conta própria e acione as equipes especializadas.

articles.title: A ideia de 50 anos que ajuda Curitiba a prevenir enchentes | G1
articles.standfirst: Especialista em cidades inteligentes explica como parques-esponja, testados há mais de 50 anos em Curitiba, ajudam municípios brasileiros a enfrentar o clima com pouco orçamento.
articles.summary: Especialista em cidades inteligentes explica como parques-esponja, testados há mais de 50 anos em Curitiba, ajudam municípios brasileiros a enfrentar o clima com pouco orçamento.
articles.body:
À medida que mais gente migra para as cidades, cresce também a pressão sobre serviços públicos como saneamento, mobilidade e prevenção a desastres. A estimativa é que, em 2050, até 70% da população mundial viva em áreas urbanas. É nesse cenário que o conceito de ‘cidade inteligente’ ganhou força nos últimos anos.

Mas usar tecnologia e dados para gerir uma cidade não significa resolver todos os seus problemas de uma única vez. Segundo Beto Marcelino, sócio fundador e presidente do Grupo iCities, empresa brasileira de inovação em cidades inteligentes, eventos climáticos extremos seguem sendo um desafio mesmo para as cidades mais avançadas do mundo.

“O processo de transformação que as cidades passam hoje em dia ocorre pela grande demanda de serviços públicos, afetada diretamente pelo maior número de pessoas que moram em áreas urbanas. Logicamente, o termo 'cidade inteligente' não quer dizer que são cidades plenas, cidades com seus problemas resolvidos e, muito menos, cidades sem problemas”, explica ele.

“Toda cidade tem muitos problemas, no Brasil e no mundo, porque você nunca consegue atender a população de maneira uniforme” , pondera.

Segundo o especialista em cidades inteligentes, a virada de chave passa pela digitalização, o uso de dados e da tecnologia para antecipar problemas, “seja de vias, esgoto ou segurança” , antes que eles se agravem. Ele cita sistemas climáticos que preveem chuvas fortes, alagamentos e desmoronamentos, além de semáforos inteligentes e sistemas que preveem picos de tráfego.

Uma realidade mais próxima do ideal pode ser encontrada na Suíça, com histórico metodológico de centenas de anos, diferente do continente americano, que ainda passa por transformações nas cidades para atender a população.

Eventos climáticos extremos, como ventos fortes, granizo e alagamentos, não são novidade, mas dois fatores agravam seus efeitos hoje: mais gente morando em áreas urbanas e a pavimentação.

O inverno de 2026 no Paraná terminou com chuva acima da média. Entre junho e agosto, a Defesa Civil estadual contabilizou 228 ocorrências de tempo severo em 150 municípios, e 39 cidades decretaram situação de emergência. Em setembro, 33 estações do Sistema de Tecnologia e Monitoramento Ambiental do Paraná (Simepar) já haviam superado a média de chuva do mês até o último domingo (20).

“A gente paga o preço quando um efeito climático acumula um volume de água muito forte naquela região” , diz Marcelino. Chuvas acima de 50 mm ou 60 mm costumam gerar escoamento não uniforme e alagamentos.

A resposta passa por duas frentes, envolvendo uma pavimentação mais permeável, com cimentos e concretos que aumentam a absorção de água, e estações climáticas inteligentes, capazes de gerar alertas em tempo real diante de mudanças bruscas de vento, umidade ou volume de chuva acumulada, dando tempo para a Defesa Civil agir antes do desastre.

Em fevereiro, Curitiba recebeu o primeiro alerta de emergência por cell broadcast, quando o Simepar identificou risco de rajadas de até 80 km/h e chance de granizo. A tempestade chegou a afetar cerca de 8,8 mil pessoas com quedas de energia, mas o alerta deu tempo para medidas preventivas antes do pior do temporal.

Um exemplo semelhante é no Rio de Janeiro, que conta com a Defesa Civil para enviar alertas automáticos para o celular da população em caso de situações classificadas como de risco severo ou extremo.

Ainda assim, há casos de cidades tidas como referência também já foram pegas de surpresa. Em Zurique, na Suíça, uma tempestade recente registrou ventos de até 140 km/h, gerou mais de 400 chamadas aos serviços de emergência da cidade e interrompeu trens e ônibus por causa de ruas alagadas.

Em outro episódio, uma chuva de granizo chegou a contaminar a rede de água potável de duas localidades e interrompeu por meia hora as operações do aeroporto da cidade.

“Não só Copenhague, mas outras cidades vêm passando por problemas graves. A própria Zurique, na Suíça, assustou muito os moradores recentemente com uma chuva fortíssima. Eventos raros que combinam chuva, vento e granizo causam problemas severos ao comércio, às pessoas, ao trânsito e ao turismo” , diz Marcelino.

Parque Barigui em Curitiba (PR). — Foto: Prefeitura de Curitiba/Divulgação.

A pergunta que fica é se uma resposta de longo prazo, como as adotadas por cidades europeias, é viável para uma cidade brasileira, com orçamento bem menor.

“Com certeza” , responde ele. E aponta um exemplo que já existe no país. A rede de mais de 50 parques criada por Jaime Lerner em Curitiba há mais de cinco décadas, muitos deles funcionando como ‘parques-esponja’, construídos no próprio leito de rios como o de Barigui.

O modelo remonta a 1972, quando o então prefeito Jaime Lerner inaugurou o Parque Barigui como um ‘parque linear’, com a função de preservar a vegetação e conter as enchentes do rio, solução depois repetida em outros pontos da cidade.

Curitiba soma hoje 54 parques e bosques públicos e aumentou em 6 metros quadrados de área verde por habitante, bem acima do mínimo de 12 metros quadrados recomendado pela Organização das Nações Unidas (ONU).

Um exemplo mais recente da mesma lógica é a Bacia de Detenção do Rio Mossunguê, no bairro Campo Comprido, inaugurada em março para funcionar como área de lazer e contenção de cheias na zona oeste da cidade.

Bacia de Detenção do Rio Mossunguê. — Foto: Ricardo Marajó/SECOM.

“Ao criar um parque ao redor do rio, você afasta as casas e os loteamentos daquela margem, dando espaço para o rio transbordar e funcionar como uma bacia de drenagem natural” , explica Marcelino.

Os parques Barigui, Tingui, Tanguá e Atuba cumprem exatamente essa função. Quando chove, o rio sobe dentro da área do parque em vez de invadir residências, e depois retorna ao normal.

“Essa é uma atitude que não custa tanto” , resume. “Essa solução de infraestrutura verde está muito em voga hoje em dia, sendo uma alternativa plenamente viável para a realidade brasileira e fundamental diante dos crescentes impactos climáticos” , conclui.

Isso mostra que apesar dos desafios enfrentados pelas cidades diante das mudanças climáticas, a natureza ainda pode ser uma aliada na prevenção de enchentes, inundações e impactos ambientais extremos.

articles.title: Temporal no RS afeta 54 mil, fere 4 pessoas e danifica 8,1 mil casas | G1
articles.standfirst: Balanço da Defesa Civil divulgado no final desta terça-feira (29) ainda mostra que são 6,2 mil desalojados.
articles.summary: O temporal no RS deixou 6,2 mil desalojados e 4 feridos, com danos em mais de 8 mil residências e escolas após chuvas de granizo e ventos fortes.
articles.body:
O número de moradores do Rio Grande do Sul atingidos pelo temporal segue crescendo. Balanço da Defesa Civil divulgado no final desta terça-feira (29) aponta que são mais de 54 mil pessoas afetadas, 6,2 mil desalojados e 8,1 mil casas danificadas.

Os dados ainda mostram que há quatro feridos. Desde domingo, diferentes regiões do estado enfrentam prejuízos em razão de chuva de granizo e vento forte.

Em São Luiz Gonzaga , um morador gravou imagens de uma forte tempestade na noite de segunda-feira (28). Meteorologistas dizem que não é possível confirmar a formação de um tornado no vídeo. Os profissionais confirmam que a região foi atingida por uma "supercélula" de tempestade.

As informações foram confirmadas pelo g1 com meteorologistas da Climatempo Meteorologia e da Defesa Civil estadual. Veja o vídeo acima .

🌪️ De acordo com a Climatempo, uma supercélula é "uma tempestade muito organizada, marcada por uma corrente de ar ascendente que permanece ativa e gira". Já um tornado é uma corrente de ar ascendente gerada entre a base da supercélula e o solo, em forma de funil, com movimento giratório

O Rio Grande do Sul registra desde segunda-feira (28) alagamentos, bloqueios em estradas, retirada de famílias e milhares de imóveis sem energia.

articles.title: Quaest: veja como está a disputa pelo governo do RJ | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e ouviu 1.302 eleitores do estado do Rio de Janeiro entre 25 e 28 de setembro. Margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais.
articles.summary: Levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo e ouviu 1.302 eleitores do estado do Rio de Janeiro entre 25 e 28 de setembro. Margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais.
articles.body:
Pesquisa Quaest divulgada nesta terça-feira (29) mostra Eduardo Paes ( PSD ) com 34% das intenções de voto para o governo do Rio de Janeiro. Douglas Ruas ( PL ) aparece com 25%. O levantamento foi encomendado pela Globo.

Na comparação com a pesquisa anterior, divulgada em 23 de setembro, Paes passou de 36% para 34%, enquanto Ruas foi de 23% para 25%. A diferença entre os dois, que era de 13 pontos percentuais, agora é de 9 pontos .

Garotinho ( Republicanos ) aparece com 9%, ante 8% na rodada anterior.

A Quaest também testou um cenário sem o nome de Garotinho, que teve a candidatura indeferida pelo Tribunal Regional Eleitoral (TRE-RJ) e pode recorrer ao Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE). Nesse cenário, Paes tem 35%, e Ruas, 26%.

A pesquisa foi contratada pela Globo. A Quaest ouviu 1.302 eleitores de 16 anos ou mais entre 25 e 28 de setembro. A margem de erro é de 3 pontos percentuais, para mais ou para menos, e o nível de confiança é de 95%. O levantamento foi registrado no Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) sob o protocolo RJ-04419/2026.

articles.title: Disney demite centenas de funcionários, diz revista | G1
articles.standfirst: Cortes atingem principalmente áreas de recursos humanos e tecnologia da informação e são a terceira rodada de demissões neste ano.
articles.summary: Cortes atingem principalmente áreas de recursos humanos e tecnologia da informação e são a terceira rodada de demissões neste ano.
articles.body:
Disney corta empregos em meio à crise — Foto: REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

A Walt Disney demitiu algumas centenas de funcionários em diferentes áreas da empresa , informou a revista americana Variety nesta terça-feira (29), citando uma fonte familiarizada com o assunto.

Os cortes atingem principalmente os departamentos de recursos humanos e tecnologia da informação (TI) , tanto na estrutura corporativa quanto em diferentes divisões.

Esta é a terceira rodada de demissões da Disney neste ano desde que Josh D'Amaro assumiu o cargo de CEO, em março. As demissões ocorrem após a empresa sinalizar que faria novos cortes de custos.

Na divulgação dos resultados do trimestre encerrado em junho, D'Amaro e o diretor financeiro Hugh Johnston afirmaram que a companhia avaliava medidas para reduzir despesas, incluindo o quadro de funcionários e gastos administrativos.

Em carta aos acionistas, divulgada em 5 de agosto, os executivos disseram que a redução de custos tinha como objetivo liberar recursos para investimentos em áreas de crescimento.

Em abril, a Disney eliminou cerca de 1.000 postos de trabalho em diferentes áreas , incluindo marketing, estúdios, televisão, ESPN, produtos e tecnologia e funções corporativas .

Em julho, houve uma nova rodada de cortes, com centenas de demissões em áreas corporativas e divisões como Pixar, ESPN e Disney Entertainment Television.

Segundo a Variety, a maior parte dos cortes nos estúdios ocorreu na Pixar, enquanto a National Geographic concentrou a maior parte das demissões na área de televisão.

Em agosto, a empresa também ofereceu pacotes de aposentadoria antecipada a executivos com muitos anos de casa.

A Disney empregava cerca de 231 mil pessoas no fim do ano fiscal de 2025 , sendo aproximadamente 172 mil nos Estados Unidos e 59 mil fora do país , segundo dados da companhia citados pela Reuters.

A Disney não respondeu imediatamente ao pedido de comentário da Reuters.

A companhia também passou por uma grande rodada de demissões em 2023, quando anunciou o corte de cerca de 7.000 empregos como parte de um plano para reduzir US$ 5,5 bilhões em custos durante a gestão do então CEO Bob Iger.

As demissões desta terça-feira (29) foram divulgadas inicialmente pelo site especializado Deadline e posteriormente confirmadas pela Variety.

articles.title: Parque dos EUA fecha montanha-russa extrema após denúncia de danos | G1
articles.standfirst: Atração X2, uma das montanhas-russas mais conhecidas do parque de diversões Six Flags, na Califórnia, está ligada a dezenas de incidentes, segundo investigação da CNN Internacional. Direção do parque disse que encerrará operações da atração, ativa desde 2008.
articles.summary: O parque de diversões Six Flags, famoso nos EUA por suas montanhas-russas, anunciou que fechará a atração X2 após denúncias de lesões cerebrais graves e mortes.
articles.body:
Fachada do parque Six Flag Magic Mountain, na Califórnia — Foto: By Jeremy Thompson from United States of America - Six Flags Magic Mountain, CC BY 2.0

O parque de diversões Six Flags, famoso nos Estados Unidos por suas montanhas-russas, anunciou nesta terça-feira (29) que fechará a atração X2 após denúncias de lesões cerebrais graves e até mortes.

As denúncias vieram à tona após uma investigação da rede de TV CNN Internacional.

➡️ Classificada como uma "montanha-russa extrema" , a X2 era uma das atrações mais conhecidas do Six Flags , cadeia de parques de diversões especializados em brinquedos radicais. Segundo a CNN Internacional, a X2 está ligada a casos de lesões graves, hospitalizações e até mortes de pessoas que usaram a atração ao longo de um período de quase duas décadas ( leia mais abaixo ).

O encerramento da atração foi anunciado em comunicado assinado por Brian Oerding, presidente do Six Flags Magic Mountain, parque que abrigava a X2, situado na Califórnia, nos EUA.

"Embora a X2 tenha sido aprovada consistentemente em inúmeros testes de segurança, decidimos encerrar as operações da atração por acreditarmos ser a decisão correta", disse Oerding. "Desde a sua inauguração em 2008, a X2 recebeu mais de 16 milhões de visitantes e conquistou uma legião de fãs apaixonados entre os entusiastas de montanhas-russas".

Os casos mais recentes de visitantes da X2 que sofreram lesões foram os de duas mulheres que tiveram que ser submetidas a cirurgias de emergência com hemorragia cerebral após andarem na atração.

"Entre as vítimas estão pessoas que sofreram deficiências que mudaram suas vidas, entraram em coma e duas que morreram em decorrência dos ferimentos", afirmou a reportagem da CNN Internacional.

👉 Os incidentes se assemelham ao caso de uma brasileira que perdeu os movimentos após andar em uma atração no Hopi Hari, parque no interior de São Paulo. O Ministério Público do Estado abriu investigação.

Os relatos à TV norte-americana foram similares aos da história contada por João Pedro Bossoni, marido da vítima da atração do Hopi Hari, ao Fantástico ( veja no vídeo abaixo ): o turista apresenta sintomas extremos, como tontura, desmaios ou até convulsões por ter batido a cabeça durante uma viagem de montanha-russa , e depois tem que ser encaminhado com urgência para o hospital.

Especialistas ouvidos pela CNN Internacional afirmaram que o risco de lesões cerebrais traumáticas associadas a montanhas-russas é considerado muito baixo, porém não há razão para um brinquedo ser projetado sem os devidos requisitos para evitar tais incidentes.

articles.title: Apple avalia reformulação para lançar produtos mais rápido, diz site  | G1
articles.standfirst: Novo CEO, John Ternus, estuda reduzir cargos de gerência e mudar calendário de lançamentos para tornar empresa mais enxuta e acelerar inovação.
articles.summary: Novo CEO, John Ternus, estuda reduzir cargos de gerência e mudar calendário de lançamentos para tornar empresa mais enxuta e acelerar inovação.
articles.body:
O CEO da Apple, John Ternus, segura um iPhone 18 Pro na loja da Apple na Quinta Avenida, em Nova York, durante o lançamento do modelo e do iPhone 18 Pro Max, em 18 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Jeenah Moon

O novo diretor-executivo da Apple, John Ternus , está avaliando uma ampla reformulação na fabricante do iPhone para dar mais foco à engenharia, lançar produtos com maior frequência e tornar a estrutura da empresa mais enxuta , informou a Bloomberg News nesta terça-feira (29).

Entre as primeiras ideias em análise estão a mudança do tradicional calendário de lançamentos de produtos, concentrado em setembro , e a redução de cargos de gerência intermediária.

A medida teria como objetivo aproximar os engenheiros dos principais executivos da companhia , segundo a reportagem, que citou fontes familiarizadas com o assunto.

Ternus é veterano da Apple , onde trabalha há 25 anos. Ele comandava a área de hardware havia vários anos e supervisionou diferentes gerações do iPhone.

Ele sucedeu Tim Cook no cargo de CEO no ínicio deste mês . Analistas afirmaram que a mudança no comando reforçou a importância dos produtos e dispositivos da Apple para o crescimento da empresa.

Segundo a Bloomberg News, a Apple já iniciou esforços para reduzir custos. Ternus também busca novas fontes de receita e maneiras de aumentar o retorno obtido com produtos que a empresa já oferece.

A Apple não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido de comentário da Reuters.

Ainda de acordo com a Bloomberg News, Ternus sinalizou internamente que a Apple precisa lançar produtos mais rapidamente e testar novas ideias para se manter competitiva na era da inteligência artificial .

A empresa costuma realizar grandes eventos anuais em junho e setembro. Em junho, acontece a conferência de desenvolvedores, voltada principalmente para novidades de software. Já em setembro, o foco costuma ser o lançamento de novos iPhones e outros dispositivos.

No início deste mês, a Apple entrou no mercado de smartphones dobráveis com o iPhone Duo , com preços que partem de R$ 21.999 e vão R$ 30.999 . ( veja todos os preços )

Analistas afirmaram que a entrada da empresa nesse segmento pode ajudar a popularizar os aparelhos dobráveis, assim como ocorreu com os smartwatches e os fones de ouvido sem fio.

A divisão de engenharia de hardware da Apple também começou a reduzir cargos de gerência responsáveis pela coordenação de projetos, segundo a Bloomberg News. As mudanças atingiram vários gerentes, incluindo cerca de meia dúzia de diretores.

A empresa também fez cortes significativos nas equipes responsáveis pela assistente digital Siri, pelo headset Vision Pro e pelo desenvolvimento de software relacionado à inteligência artificial.

Ternus também avalia como a inteligência artificial pode acelerar o desenvolvimento de produtos e automatizar tarefas que hoje são realizadas por funcionários, de acordo com a Bloomberg News.

articles.title: More than 575 Nevada volunteers worked across 26 Truckee River watershed sites and removed 120,125 pounds of waste in one day, including 2,500 pounds pulled directly from the river and 64,320 pounds of invasive weeds
articles.summary: A single day of community cleanup across Nevada’s Truckee River watershed resulted in more than 60 tons of waste being removed from public spaces,
articles.body: A single day of community cleanup across Nevada’s Truckee River watershed resulted in more than 60 tons of waste being removed from public spaces, waterways and surrounding areas. According to Keep Truckee Meadows Beautiful (KTMB), more than 575 volunteers worked across 26 sites on September 26, removing a total of 120,125 pounds of waste. The haul included 9,095 pounds of litter, 46,710 pounds of green waste and 64,320 pounds of invasive weeds. Of the litter collected, 2,500 pounds came directly from the Truckee River itself. The effort also included planting, mulching and storm-drain projects designed to protect the watershed beyond the cleanup day.Volunteers spread across 26 cleanup sitesThe annual Truckee River Cleanup was organised by KTMB, which brings volunteers together each year for projects throughout the Truckee River watershed. This year’s event took place on September 26, with volunteers working from 9 a.m. to noon at sites along the river corridor and its tributaries. KTMB’s volunteer information says the projects included trash collection, invasive weed removal, planting native vegetation and other efforts to prepare areas for the cooler months.The scale of this year’s effort was spread across 26 different locations rather than concentrated at a single stretch of the river. That allowed volunteers to address several kinds of environmental work at the same time. The results were substantial. KTMB reported that the volunteers removed 120,125 pounds of waste, equivalent to more than 60 tons. The organisation’s breakdown shows that 9,095 pounds was litter, while 46,710 pounds was green waste and another 64,320 pounds consisted of invasive weeds. The numbers also show that the cleanup was about more than picking up discarded rubbish.More than 64,000 pounds of invasive weeds removedInvasive weeds accounted for the largest individual portion of the material removed during the event. Volunteers pulled 64,320 pounds of invasive weeds, alongside 46,710 pounds of green waste. Together, those two categories made up more than 111,000 pounds of the total material collected. Removing invasive vegetation can be an important part of maintaining areas around waterways because unwanted plant species can compete with native vegetation and alter the character of surrounding habitats. KTMB lists invasive weed removal among its regular cleanup activities, alongside litter collection and other watershed projects.The organisation's cleanup programme also aims to prepare public areas for the changing seasons. Rather than treating waste collection as an isolated activity, volunteers worked on several aspects of the landscape at the same time. This included planting seven trees and 171 other plants. Volunteers also spread 115 yards of mulch in parks and other areas targeted for beautification.2,500 pounds of litter came directly from the riverThe cleanup also focused specifically on material that had already reached the Truckee River. Of the 9,095 pounds of litter collected overall, volunteers removed 2,500 pounds directly from the river. KTMB says the work is intended to help prevent litter and potentially hazardous materials from remaining in or reaching the river. This figure provides perspective on the different challenges involved in protecting a watershed. Waste lying in parks, along paths or in open spaces can eventually be carried into waterways by rainfall and runoff.Removing it before that happens can therefore be part of broader watershed protection. The volunteers also worked on storm drains. Across the cleanup sites, they stencilled 201 storm drains as a way of helping prevent hazardous waste from being dumped into the river. That work is less immediately visible than filling bags with rubbish, but it addresses one of the pathways through which pollutants can enter the water system.A cleanup that goes beyond collecting trashThe Truckee River Cleanup has become an annual community effort. According to KTMB, it has organised the event since 2004, bringing volunteers together for litter removal, weed pulling, storm-drain stencilling and park beautification across the watershed. In 2025, more than 550 volunteers removed nearly 25 tons of trash and green waste. The 2026 results therefore represent a much larger one-day collection than the previous year's reported total, although the material categories and reporting methods should not be assumed to be identical. Local news outlet KRNV reported that more than 575 volunteers participated across the watershed and described the preliminary results as more than 60 tons of trash, along with more than 55.5 tons of weeds and green waste. The report also confirmed the 2,500-pound river litter figure and the additional planting and storm-drain work. For KTMB, the event is designed not simply as a large-scale rubbish collection but as a way to bring residents, organisations, businesses and local authorities together around the watershed.With 120,125 pounds of material removed in a single day, the 2026 cleanup showed how many different tasks can contribute to caring for a river system. Trash was taken out of the water, invasive plants were removed from surrounding areas, new vegetation was planted and storm drains were marked to help protect the river in the future. The result was a cleanup that addressed both what was already damaging the landscape and some of the routes through which new waste could reach the Truckee River.You use AI every day. articles.title: Motorcycle patrols swarm Iranian cities, checkpoints rise as regime braces for unrest
articles.summary: Sources told Fox News Digital that IRGC, Basij and police have flooded Tehran with checkpoints and patrols as student protests over compulsory hijab grow.
articles.body: Iranian security forces have stepped up their presence in Tehran and other cities, with motorcycle patrols, checkpoints and forces positioned across major urban areas as authorities brace for possible unrest, multiple sources inside Iran told Fox News Digital. The security buildup comes as university students have returned to the streets in Tehran, protesting compulsory hijab rules, rising education costs and political repression, videos published on Iran International show. Sources inside Iran confirmed to Fox News Digital that motorcycle units have been operating across Tehran and other cities during events surrounding Iran’s annual "Sacred Defense Week," while members of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Basij and law enforcement have been positioned at major squares and other locations. IRAN INSTALLS NEW WAR CHIEFS AS TEHRAN SIGNALS ‘PROLONGED CONFRONTATION,’ EXPERT WARNS The sources also said security personnel have stopped pedestrians, searched some individuals and examined mobile phones, including material authorities consider "anti-regime." The accounts follow a report from the National Council of Resistance of Iran’s (NCRI's) Committee on Security and Counterterrorism alleging that Iranian authorities ordered a "100%" state of readiness for the Army, IRGC, Basij and law enforcement and canceled leave through Sept. 27. The NCRI also claimed 51,000 personnel had been deployed across Greater Tehran, including 30,000 IRGC and Basij members and 21,000 law enforcement personnel. The reported preparations are taking place as signs of public unrest have begun resurfacing on university campuses. Fox News Digital has not independently confirmed those claims. One source in Tehran told Fox News Digital that the heightened security presence extends beyond what is visible on the streets. INSIDE TEHRAN: IRANIANS DESCRIBE IRGC'S BRUTAL RULE, POVERTY — ASK TRUMP TO 'STAY THE COURSE' "Motorcyclists taking photos of shops, and prisoners being threatened and forced to tell their families not to physically participate in any protests that might arise," the source said. The source said Basij members who previously received military training have been placed on alert and are being housed or assembled at educational facilities and large properties on the outskirts of Tehran. The measures were not limited to the capital. "This situation exists in all cities, but the nature of the presence and the way things are organized differ," the source told Fox News Digital, citing information received from Borujen, Isfahan and other cities. IRAN ACCELERATES EXECUTION CAMPAIGN AGAINST ANTI-REGIME ACTIVISTS AMID INTERNET CENSORSHIP "In those places, plainclothes agents are more prevalent and try to remain out of public view; however, in Tehran, they appear openly on the streets in military uniforms and gear specifically to instill fear and terror," the source said, adding that leave had also been canceled in smaller cities and claimed shops, telephone communications and everyday activities were under increased surveillance. Iranian journalist Mehdi Ghadimi, who lives outside Iran after years of opposition activity, separately told Fox News Digital that he had received similar accounts. "I’ve received reports of new checkpoints being set up in Tehran, and there have also been reports of military forces being put on alert, as well as civilians who had previously been trained by the regime for urban repression being called up," Ghadimi added that people are being detained on espionage charges simply because they communicate with people outside of Iran. IRAN INMATES SEW LIPS SHUT IN MASS HUNGER STRIKE AT NOTORIOUS US-SANCTIONED JAIL: REPORT Ghadimi also said he had received reports that individuals with serious criminal records had been released from prison in exchange for reporting to local Basij bases and participating in the suppression of demonstrations. Students at Allameh Tabataba’i University in Tehran held a protest Monday against compulsory hijab, rising tuition and university living conditions, according to videos reported by Iran International on Sept. 28 and 29. Students were recorded chanting against the morality police and political repression. Iran International reported that the protest began over tuition, dormitory and food costs before expanding into broader political chants. The outlet, citing the student publication Amirkabir, reported that Basij members attempted to disrupt the gathering and threatened students. IRAN'S REGIME CAME FOR TEENAGE TWINS. THEIR FATE OFFERS A GLIMPSE OF TEHRAN'S WIDENING DEATH CAMPAIGN The protests also come amid renewed pressure over compulsory hijab rules on university campuses. On Sept. 8, Iran International reported that a senior official in the office representing Iran’s supreme leader at universities said a new compulsory-hijab directive for universities had been drafted and was expected to be issued by the ministries overseeing higher education. Separately, the IRGC escalated its rhetoric toward Washington on Tuesday, with spokesman Hossein Mohebbi calling on Americans to pressure President Donald Trump’s administration. "This lying administration must be changed," Mohebbi said at a Tehran press conference, according to Reuters video distributed Sept. 29. His remarks came as U.S. and Iranian officials continued indirect contacts through mediators in an effort to end the seven-month conflict, Reuters reported. The combination of visible security preparations and renewed demonstrations is fueling speculation among Iranians about whether the country could face another broader wave of unrest. articles.title: How Joe Biden averted a wider war with Iran: Explained in 10 points
articles.summary: Former US Middle East coordinator Brett McGurk recounts how Biden’s administration coordinated with Israel and regional allies to intercept Iran’s
articles.body: Former US Middle East coordinator Brett McGurk recounts how Biden’s administration coordinated with Israel and regional allies to intercept Iran’s unprecedented missile attack in April 2024, while attempting to prevent the crisis from escalating into a regional war.The United States helped avert a wider Middle East conflict in April 2024 by coordinating an unprecedented multinational military effort to defend Israel against Iran’s missile and drone attack, according to former US Middle East coordinator Brett McGurk.In an account adapted from his forthcoming book Brink: Inside the Race to Free the October 7th Hostages, published by The Atlantic, McGurk detailed how President Joe Biden navigated deteriorating relations with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, stalled hostage negotiations, Iranian-backed militia attacks and the threat of direct confrontation between Tehran and Tel Aviv.McGurk, who was closely involved in hostage negotiations alongside CIA Director William Burns, described how the US administration eventually used its military capabilities and diplomatic leverage to contain the Iranian attack and discourage Israel from launching an immediate counterstrike.Here is how Biden administration worked to prevent the crisis from escalating into a wider war.1. Gaza hostage negotiations stalled as regional tensions escalatedAccording to McGurk’s account in The Atlantic, Biden had asked him shortly after Hamas’s October 7, 2023, attack on Israel to help negotiate a cease-fire and hostage-release agreement.The first breakthrough came in November 2023, when a seven-day truce resulted in the release of more than 100 Israeli hostages, including women and children, in exchange for hundreds of Palestinian prisoners held by Israel. Humanitarian assistance also entered Gaza during the pause in fighting, McGurk wrote.However, negotiations collapsed on December 1 after Hamas refused to release younger women hostages as agreed and instead proposed moving directly to discussions over older male captives.Israel rejected the proposal, and fighting resumed.McGurk said Hamas subsequently demanded a return to the pre-October 7 status quo, including retaining control over Gaza. Israel, under Netanyahu, rejected the possibility of Hamas continuing to govern the territory.By February 2024, the war had entered its fifth month, with nearly 30,000 Palestinians reported killed, including militants, according to the figures cited by McGurk. More than 230 Israeli soldiers had also died, while Hamas continued to hold over 100 hostages.2. Iranian-backed attacks on US forces pushed Washington towards confrontationWhile Washington attempted to revive hostage negotiations, attacks by Iranian-backed militias against American forces in Iraq and Syria intensified.McGurk wrote that attacks against US troops had increased sevenfold since October 7 compared with the previous year, with several strikes aimed at killing American personnel.On Christmas Day 2023, three US personnel were wounded in an attack in northern Iraq, one of them seriously.Days later, Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi group began targeting commercial shipping and military vessels in the Red Sea.According to McGurk, Biden subsequently asked him to meet Iranian representatives in Oman through an existing diplomatic back channel. The meeting was intended to communicate Washington's concerns and prevent further escalation.However, the diplomatic effort failed to produce an agreement.On January 28, 2024, an Iranian-supplied drone struck the living quarters of American troops in Jordan, killing three US soldiers and injuring dozens.Biden responded by ordering what McGurk described as the largest wave of American air strikes across Iraq and Syria in more than a decade.The strikes targeted militia infrastructure, including the leader held responsible for the Jordan attack and an Iranian adviser in Baghdad who was supporting the militias.McGurk said the militias subsequently stopped attacking American forces.3. Biden attempted to bridge differences between Israel and HamasIn February 2024, McGurk returned to Cairo to revive the hostage negotiations with Egypt's intelligence chief Abbas Kamel and Israeli negotiators led by Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar.According to McGurk's account, the discussions initially appeared to have little chance of success because Israel and Hamas maintained fundamentally different positions.Hamas, through its leadership in Gaza, demanded a complete Israeli withdrawal, a permanent cease-fire and the release of all Palestinian prisoners in Israeli jails.Israel rejected these conditions.McGurk and CIA Director William Burns subsequently developed a compromise proposal focused on releasing a humanitarian category of hostages, including women, elderly people and the sick or wounded, in exchange for Palestinian prisoners.The proposal covered more than 30 hostages, including three Americans.In return, Hamas would receive a cease-fire lasting at least six weeks, with the possibility of extending it while negotiations continued over the remaining captives.Israeli negotiator Ronen Bar indicated that Israel could accept the broad framework, McGurk wrote.However, Egyptian intelligence chief Kamel warned that Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar was unlikely to agree.The negotiations eventually stalled again, with Hamas rejecting the proposed compromise and maintaining its original demands.4. Netanyahu's Rafah offensive threatened to deepen the crisisMcGurk's account describes how Israel's preparations for a major offensive in Rafah, southern Gaza, became another obstacle to negotiations.During the February Cairo meeting, Bar informed the mediators that Israel was preparing its largest military operation of the war in Rafah.According to McGurk, Israeli intelligence believed Hamas remained militarily organised in the area, with brigades, battalions and an extensive tunnel network.Rafah was also sheltering large numbers of Palestinians displaced by Israeli military operations elsewhere in Gaza.Bar argued that the only way to stop the planned offensive was for Hamas to begin releasing hostages.During a subsequent meeting in Jerusalem, Netanyahu told McGurk that Hamas's continued presence near Israel's borders posed an existential security concern.The Israeli prime minister also indicated that if a Gaza agreement could not be reached, Israel might consider military action against Hezbollah in Lebanon to secure its northern border.McGurk wrote that Netanyahu was primarily focused on eliminating Hamas's military capabilities and believed that continued military pressure would eventually force Sinwar to release the hostages.The US negotiator, however, remained concerned that military escalation could further complicate the hostage negotiations.5. US-Israel tensions intensified over the Gaza warBy March 2024, Biden was facing growing domestic political pressure over Israel's military operations and the humanitarian situation in Gaza.According to McGurk, the president was under criticism from sections of his own Democratic Party for continuing military support to Israel.Earlier that month, Biden described Israel's planned Rafah operation as a “red line” in an interview, saying Israel “must pay more attention to the innocent lives being lost.”Vice President Kamala Harris also described the proposed Rafah operation as a “huge mistake” and did not rule out consequences if Israel proceeded.However, McGurk wrote that Biden later clarified that his comments concerned how Israel conducted the operation, rather than whether it should take place.The growing differences between Washington and Jerusalem coincided with the collapse of hostage negotiations.On March 18, Biden called Netanyahu and urged him to offer more Palestinian prisoners as part of the proposed agreement. Netanyahu reluctantly agreed, but Hamas did not change its position, according to McGurk.The United States subsequently abstained from a United Nations Security Council vote on a resolution calling for an unconditional cease-fire in Gaza during Ramadan, allowing it to pass.McGurk said Hamas viewed the resolution as a diplomatic opportunity and used Israel's growing international isolation to reinforce its negotiating position.Israeli negotiators eventually withdrew from the talks.6. Israel's Damascus strike brought Iran and Israel closer to direct confrontationThe crisis took a new turn on April 1, 2024, when Israel launched an air strike in Damascus, killing senior Iranian military commander Mohammad Reza Zahedi and several associates.According to McGurk, Zahedi was a senior Iranian officer responsible for proxy operations across Syria and Lebanon, including support for Hezbollah.Before the attack, Israeli military officials had informed McGurk that the operation was imminent.One Israeli official also warned that Iran might describe the targeted building as a consulate, although Israel maintained that it had no evidence that the facility was a diplomatic mission.After the strike, Iran declared that it considered the attack an assault on Iranian territory and vowed retaliation against Israel.McGurk wrote that American intelligence subsequently began receiving reports of Iranian preparations for a large-scale missile and drone attack against Israeli cities.The potential scale of the retaliation alarmed Washington.Iran had traditionally relied on regional proxy groups to confront Israel and the United States, allowing Tehran to maintain some distance from direct military confrontation.However, the planned attack appeared to represent a departure from that approach.According to McGurk, US officials assessed that Iran was preparing to launch hundreds of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and drones towards Israel.7. Biden approved US military deployment despite deteriorating ties with NetanyahuAs Iran's preparations became clearer, Israel formally requested American military assistance to defend its territory.McGurk described the request as extraordinary because it departed from Israel's traditional military doctrine: We defend ourselves, by ourselves.Israel sought American assistance involving air wings, destroyers and missile-defence systems.At the same time, Biden's relationship with Netanyahu was deteriorating.McGurk wrote that the two leaders had spoken only a handful of times during the first quarter of 2024, compared with nearly 20 conversations during the final quarter of 2023.The relationship further deteriorated after Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer called for elections in Israel and Netanyahu's replacement.Against this backdrop, Biden held a meeting with senior advisers, including Secretary of State Antony Blinken, CIA Director William Burns and national security adviser Jake Sullivan, on April 4.According to McGurk, Biden approved the emergency deployment of additional American military forces to the region on the recommendation of Defence Secretary Lloyd Austin.The president also discussed whether the United States should threaten to suspend military assistance to Israel to pressure Netanyahu into ending the Gaza war.However, Biden questioned the consequences of such a move while Israel faced attacks from multiple directions and hostages remained in Hamas captivity.“We’re on the side of Iran?” he asked rhetorically, according to McGurk.8. Biden confronted Netanyahu and linked Iran's defence to ending the Gaza warDuring the April 4 telephone conversation with Netanyahu, Biden expressed frustration over Israel's handling of the humanitarian crisis and the continuing military campaign in Gaza.According to McGurk, the president opened the call by asking: “Bibi, man, what the fuck are you doing?”Biden warned that the United States could withdraw military assistance, while Netanyahu responded that Israel would defend itself even without American support.The discussion also covered the killing of seven World Central Kitchen aid workers in an Israeli drone strike in northern Gaza on April 1.Biden demanded concrete steps to improve humanitarian access, including opening additional crossings into northern Gaza.When Netanyahu attempted to explain Israel's preliminary assessment of the incident, Biden interrupted him.“I don’t want to hear it, Bibi.”According to McGurk, Biden then made clear that the United States would help defend Israel against Iran but expected immediate efforts to end the Gaza war and secure the release of hostages.“That’s the deal, pal.”Following the call, the White House issued a statement warning that US policy would be determined by its assessment of Israel's immediate actions regarding civilian harm, humanitarian suffering and the safety of aid workers.At the same time, the statement reaffirmed American support for Israel against Iranian threats.McGurk described this as the central dilemma confronting the Biden administration: Washington wanted to pressure Israel over Gaza without weakening its defence against Iran.9. US-led multinational military operation intercepted Iran's unprecedented attackOn April 13, 2024, Iran launched its first direct large-scale attack against Israel from its own territory.According to McGurk's account, the attack began at approximately 3:30 pm with around 200 drones, followed roughly 90 minutes later by 30 cruise missiles.Iran subsequently launched more than 100 ballistic missiles in multiple waves.The attack was designed to overwhelm Israeli air defences by ensuring that drones, cruise missiles and ballistic missiles arrived around the same time, McGurk wrote.The United States had spent the preceding 96 hours strengthening Israel's defences, deploying additional military assets and coordinating with Arab and European countries.During the attack, American fighter aircraft intercepted Iranian drones over Syria, Iraq and Saudi Arabia, while US Navy destroyers and regional air-defence systems helped counter incoming threats.McGurk described how US and Israeli defence systems worked together to intercept the incoming projectiles.Israel's Arrow systems engaged ballistic missiles at high altitudes, while American destroyers fired SM-3 interceptors to destroy incoming threats above the atmosphere.US Army Patriot batteries across the Middle East were also placed on alert.According to McGurk, American pilots Lieutenant Colonel Kevin Murphy and Major George Welton, along with their squadron, shot down around two dozen Iranian drones.The operation involved American military forces working alongside Israeli forces and a coalition of European and Arab countries.As the attack unfolded, General Erik Kurilla, who was overseeing US military operations, informed Biden that the number of ballistic missiles launched had increased through successive waves.McGurk recalled that the Situation Room tracked more than 100 Iranian ballistic missiles heading towards Israel.Despite the scale of the attack, the combined air-defence effort appeared to have prevented major damage.US military officials initially reported no confirmed impacts, while Israeli authorities subsequently reported no significant impacts.McGurk noted that one young girl in southern Israel was wounded by falling shrapnel.The successful interception prevented the immediate military consequences that could have triggered an Israeli retaliatory strike against Iran.10. Biden urged Netanyahu to avoid retaliation and contain the conflictFollowing the interception operation, the immediate challenge for Washington was preventing Israel from launching a major retaliatory attack against Iran.According to McGurk, Biden wanted Netanyahu to recognise the success of the defensive operation and avoid turning it into a broader military confrontation.The president asked for Netanyahu to be brought onto a telephone call.When Netanyahu initially requested 30 minutes before speaking, Biden expressed frustration, asking whether the Israeli prime minister understood that the United States had just helped save Israel.National Security Adviser Jake Sullivan and his deputy Jon Finer subsequently prepared talking points recommending that Israel respond in a way that inflicted few casualties and prevented further escalation.During the conversation, Biden acknowledged Israel's right to respond but urged Netanyahu to coordinate with Washington and ensure that any action was designed to deter Iran rather than escalate the conflict.“Take the win,” Biden said.Netanyahu remained noncommittal, arguing that Iran needed to be taught a lesson.However, both leaders agreed that their military teams would discuss possible responses.McGurk wrote that the Biden administration subsequently received another warning from Tehran against supporting Israel in a retaliatory operation.Iran's UN mission also issued a public message stating: “US MUST STAY AWAY!!”The immediate confrontation eventually subsided, although tensions between Israel and Iran continued.The following morning, Biden spoke with the American pilots and military commanders involved in defending Israel, including Murphy and Welton's squadron.Recalling the operation, Biden told the pilots:“The only reason we’re not in a major war right now is because of what you did. I mean it, guys. Thank you, thank you, thank you. You saved the world; I mean it. God bless you.”According to McGurk, the episode demonstrated how American military coordination, regional cooperation and direct diplomatic engagement helped prevent Iran's unprecedented attack from triggering a wider regional war.However, the underlying Gaza conflict, stalled hostage negotiations and tensions between Washington and Jerusalem remained unresolved.This article is based on Brett McGurk's first-person account published in The Atlantic, adapted from his forthcoming bookBrink: Inside the Race to Free the October 7th Hostages. The military and diplomatic developments described above are attributed to McGurk's account unless otherwise specified.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Eiffel Tower chief to quit after female staff replaced by men during religious visit
articles.summary: The company that runs the Eiffel Tower said the removal of female staff during the visit earlier this month was "unacceptable".
articles.body:
The chief executive of the company that runs the Eiffel Tower will step down after a backlash over female staff being replaced by male colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group.

Patrick Branco Ruivo, who has been director general of the Paris landmark since 2018, will leave his job at the end of the year, the company SETE said in a statement.

It said an internal investigation found that "operational flaws and shortcomings" in organising the visit led to the "unacceptable" removal of female staff.

They were replaced by male colleagues as a delegation of around 100 people linked to the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) group visited the Eiffel Tower earlier this month.

BAPS - a movement whose beliefs originate in the 18th Century - strictly separates men and women, including in temple activities and building entrances.

At the time, SETE said the Hindu delegation had requested that the visit be organised so as to limit "interactions with women" and said that "these conditions should not have been accepted".

A staff union representative said "women were asked to leave their places of work" and felt "humiliated".

Staff at the monument said female employees were also "instructed not to go through or cross certain areas while the delegation was present".

The visit led to the closure of the tower as staff went on strike to show their outrage and politicians condemned the incident.

Yaël Braun-Pivet, the president of France's National Assembly, said after the visit: "I refuse to allow women to be compelled to step aside in order to meet the demands of foreign visitors."

The Socialist mayor of Paris, Emmanuel Gregoire, called it an "absurd, unjust and unacceptable decision" and ordered two separate investigations.

SETE chair Ariel Weil said on Tuesday that he had requested measures and training programmes promoting gender equality to be implemented.

"The coming months will allow us to prepare for the leadership transition under the best possible conditions," he said.

BAPS apologised "for any pain or inconvenience caused" earlier this month, adding "we believe in the universal values of mutual respect and service".

On its website, the group describes itself as a "spiritual, volunteer-driven fellowship dedicated to improving society" through Hindu values.

It has temples in major cities around the world, including London, Los Angeles and Sydney.

It draws its beliefs from the teachings of Lord Swaminarayan, a late 18th-Century celibate ascetic who is regarded by his followers as an incarnation of Vishnu, the revered Hindu god of preservation.

BAPS says the segregation of men and women was introduced for the benefit of women, but critics say 18th-Century beliefs have no place in today's world, and keeping women out in the name of religious practices is discriminatory.

articles.title: Celebrity Traitors star Michael Sheen says being an actor will be a 'disadvantage'
articles.summary: The Hollywood actor says he is a big fan of the BBC reality show, which he will now try and win.
articles.body:
Michael Sheen has said he thinks being an actor will be a disadvantage while he is on Celebrity Traitors.

The 57-year-old is among the stars who will go head to head in the second series of the BBC reality game spin-off .

A total of 21 presenters, comedians, actors and musicians will try their hand at being traitors and faithfuls in the show, which airs on 1 October.

The Hollywood actor from Port Talbot said he wanted to participate because he is a "big fan" of the show and wanted to be in the castle after previously filming in the area.

Speaking about how his public persona may affect how others perceive and treat him on the show, the actor said: "Well, I do think it's a disadvantage to be an actor because people immediately go, 'oh well, he pretends for a living'.

"I don't think that is the case, because the whole point of acting is that you have to trick yourself into believing that what you're doing is true. If you are consciously aware that you're pretending or you're saying things that aren't true, then it's bad acting. It's just bad.

"Just for me being an actor, I think that's a disadvantage because people are already suspicious of that.

"Beyond being an actor, just my persona, I don't really know what people think about me. So, I don't know if it'll help or not."

Sheen portrayed the disgraced Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor in the 2024 Prime Video series, A Very Royal Scandal.

It was based on the 2019 BBC Newsnight interview conducted by Emily Maitlis with Mountbatten-Windsor regarding his relationship with Jeffrey Epstein, and became a defining moment in modern royal and media history.

Sheen has also starred in films including Frost/Nixon, The Damned United and The Special Relationship.

Sheen said: "I knew the area a bit [where Traitors is filmed in Scotland], and it is stunningly beautiful. It's a lovely place to be and the game is just fascinating.

"I think for a show to be so popular and to grab the cultural imagination so much, it has to have the ability to go beyond what its genre is.

"It somehow speaks to something a bit deeper, maybe. People get so absorbed in it."

The first series of The Celebrity Traitors aired on the BBC last autumn, with its nail-biting finale hitting a peak of 15.4 million viewers, and Alan Carr emerging victorious .

Bringing in an average audience of 14.9 million people during its run, it received the biggest TV audience of 2025.

Fronted by Claudia Winkleman, the game is set in a Scottish castle in the Highlands, and follows the contestants - the majority of whom are known as faithfuls - as they try to seek out the murderous traitors among them, who kill off players in the middle of the night.

The celebrities will use their skills and experience to convince the other players that they are faithfuls as they try and win £100,000 for a charity of their choice.

The second celebrity version of the show will consist of 10 hour-long episodes.

Those taking part alongside Sheen include comedians Joe Lycett and Romesh Ranganathan, actors Miranda Hart and Richard E. Grant, and singer James Blunt.

The latest regular series was broadcast in January, attracting more than 12 million viewers per episode.

The Celebrity Traitors returns to BBC One and iPlayer on 1 October.

articles.title: Fatima Zahra El Mansouri named as Morocco's first female prime minister
articles.summary: Her appointment by the king makes her only the second woman to lead a government in the Arab world.
articles.body:
Fatima Zahra El Mansouri has been named Morocco's first female prime minister, after her centrist Authenticity and Modernity Party (Pam) won the most seats in last week's parliamentary elections.

Her appointment makes her only the second woman to lead a government in the Arab world, after Tunisia's Najla Bouden.

She was named by King Mohammed VI, who chose her as prime minister over the country's football chief Fouzi Lekjaa, a top politician from the same party. El Mansouri, 50, has been the mayor of Marrakesh for a number of years and also served as a minister in the previous coalition government.

Morocco is a constitutional monarchy but most power remains in the hands of the king.

How Ceuta, football and Israel shaped Morocco's election

At a victory press conference, prior to her announcement as prime minister, El Mansouri was asked whether the state would need to make changes to accommodate her in Muslim religious ceremonies attended by the king, including Friday and Eid prayers, where men and women pray in separate sections.

She did not directly answer the question, instead praising the king as "the biggest advocate for women" in the country.

"His Majesty is the holder of wisdom… If I am entrusted with the responsibility of head of government, it will be a great honour," she said.

El Mansouri is one of Morocco's most prominent female politicians.

A lawyer by training, she studied at Mohammed V University in the capital, Rabat, before continuing her education in France and the US, specialising in business and corporate law.

She entered politics after Pam was founded in 2008 and became the first woman to serve as mayor of Marrakesh in 2009. She returned to the post after the 2021 elections.

In the past five years, she served as a minister for national territory planning, urban planning, housing and city policy under former Prime Minister Aziz Akhannouch.

In February 2024, she became the co-ordinator of Pam's leadership coalition.

El Mansouri has rejected her portrayal as an "iron woman", telling Pam's magazine in 2021: "I am neither a woman of steel nor iron... I am a free activist."

During her political career, El Mansouri has rarely spoken publicly about women's rights or gender inequality, despite ongoing debates in Morocco over issues such as whether polygamy should be banned and whether men and women should have equal inheritance rights.

Under Morocco's constitution, the king appoints the head of government from the party that comes first in elections to the House of Representatives.

Pam has been led by a collective leadership since February 2024, rather than a single secretary general.

After the results were announced last week, El Mansouri said the decision was ultimately up to the king to choose between her and Lekjaa.

In the past, the appointment was largely a formality, as most Moroccan parties were led by a single secretary general, making it clear who would be nominated to head the government.

With 97 seats, Pam does not have a majority and will need to form a coalition to reach the 198 seats required for an absolute majority in the 395-member parliament.

It is not clear which party it will work with as it has fallen out with the National Rally of Independents (RNI), which led the outgoing government in which Pam was a junior partner.

The Islamist Justice and Development Party (PJD) ⁠rebounded with 54 seats, from only 13 in the previous election - buoyed by the return of party leader Abdelilah Benkirane, a former prime minister.

After the vote, Benkirane said the party would stay in opposition, refusing a partnership with Pam.

articles.title: Lindsay Clancy appears in court as her lawyer pushes for murder case dismissal
articles.summary: Clancy's defence lawyer wants her to be cleared of murdering her three children in 2023 but prosecutors say the state proved guilt.
articles.body:
Warning: This story contains distressing details and discussion of attempted suicide

Lindsay Clancy, the US woman accused of murdering her three children, has appeared in court for the first time since her murder trial fell apart earlier this month.

Her defence team on Tuesday argued the judge should dismiss her case but prosecutors said the state had "met its burden" in proving her guilt.

Clancy, 36, does not deny killing her three children in 2023, but her defence team argues she was suffering from severe postpartum psychosis at the time. Prosecutors say the killings were intentional.

It is still not clear if she will face a retrial. The request to dismiss the case is among those that will be discussed at a hearing on 2 November, Judge William Sullivan said.

One of the motions addressed on Tuesday was from Clancy's lawyer, Kevin Reddington, who asked for her to be found not guilty under Rule 25 - a Massachusetts motion that states a defendant should be found not guilty if prosecutors do not argue their case effectively.

Reddington also brought a new defence forward arguing there was not enough evidence to prove Clancy killed her children.

"This entire case is based on speculation," he said.

It was a change of argument from the defence lawyer, who during the trial focused on Clancy's mental health - urging the jury to find her not criminally responsible because of it.

Prosecutor Shanan Buckingham called Reddington's argument "laughable".

She said state prosecutors had presented numerous pieces of evidence showing Clancy was in a healthy mental state at the time of the murders during the trial.

"The Commonwealth met its burden," Buckingham said.

She argued Clancy knew what she was doing when she killed her three children, Cora, five, Dawson, three, and Callan, who was eight months, in their Massachusetts home.

Judge Sullivan pushed back when both Reddington and Buckingham refused to agree to his suggestion that they might agree to a possible retrial date now ahead of the hearing, saying he wanted to "get this thing moving".

He asked both sides to be prepared to discuss possible trial dates at the November hearing.

Reddington said he would be unable to go to trial until at least June if the case is retried.

District Attorney Timothy Cruz told reporters outside after court that prosecutors have not yet decided if they are going to retry Clancy on murder charges.

"We're doing our due diligence, we're going to continue doing that," he said. "We're going to do what we can for the children. That's what this case is about."

Following a week of deliberations earlier this month, a Massachusetts jury told Sullivan they could not reach a verdict because of a lone holdout juror and a mistrial was declared on 4 September.

articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have filed a 398-page chargesheet against a sleeper bus driver and conductor accused of gang-raping a minor during a journey from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police have filed a 398-page chargesheet against a sleeper bus driver and conductor accused of gang-raping a minor during a journey from Greater Noida to Delhi in August, with biological evidence recovered from the bus, including semen samples and hair strands, forming a key part of the case.The chargesheet also highlights multiple safety and regulatory violations by the vehicle, including a non-functional CCTV camera and absence of mandatory safety features.The chargesheet was filed before a city court on September 18, and the court took cognisance of it on September 24, police said. Minor allegedly assaulted inside sleeper busThe incident allegedly took place on the night of August 4 when the minor, a resident of Uttar Pradesh, boarded the bus in Greater Noida after being told that it was headed towards Noida Sector 63, where she wanted to go.According to police, she realised after boarding that there were no other passengers and tried to get off. The conductor allegedly stopped her from leaving and locked the door.The bus then travelled towards Delhi, where the minor was allegedly assaulted inside the vehicle before being dropped near the Kashmere Gate bus terminal. She subsequently approached police and filed a complaint.Police said they traced the bus and arrested the driver and conductor soon after.CCTV trail leads police to accusedMultiple police teams examined CCTV footage along the route and traced the bus to a parking area in Timarpur within hours, leading to the arrest of driver Kuldeep and conductor Sandeep, both residents of Kanpur.The chargesheet cites 10 police personnel, doctors and others as witnesses.During forensic examination of the bus, investigators recovered biological evidence, including alleged semen samples and hair strands. The samples were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory for examination.Bus had 11 pending challans, no panic buttonThe investigation also brought to light several safety and regulatory lapses involving the bus.The vehicle had 11 pending traffic challans, including seven issued in July for alleged overspeeding.Investigators also found that the bus's CCTV camera was non-functional and that curtains had been installed on its windows.The vehicle lacked safety features including a panic button and a vehicle tracking system, police said.Police further said the two accused had allegedly been employed without police verification.Supreme Court takes suo motu cognisanceThe case has brought back memories of the 2012 Nirbhaya incident, in which a 23-year-old physiotherapy intern was brutally raped and tortured inside a bus before being dumped on a road.The Supreme Court on Monday took suo motu cognisance of news reports about the sleeper bus incident and other crimes against minor girls and women across Delhi-NCR, observing that such cases underline a systematic failure on the part of law enforcement authorities.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said one could not help but draw painful parallels with the 2012 Nirbhaya case, raising questions over whether systemic law enforcement mechanisms had made any meaningful progress in the decade since then.(With PTI inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: RAF Fairford: 'Quantity of petrol' but no explosives found in three vehicles
articles.summary: Police say the decision to release five men on bail is one "grounded in experience and strategy".
articles.body:
A quantity of petrol but no explosive devices were found during searches of the three vans near RAF Fairford in the west of England, counter-terror police have said.

Five men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences and later terrorism offences after the vehicles were spotted in the early hours of Sunday, sparking a major security incident around the base which is operated by the US military.

They were released on bail the following day in what police described as an "investigative decision" which was "grounded in experience and strategy".

It comes after US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said it was clear a "foreign actor" had been involved, without providing evidence.

Police were alerted to "three suspicious vehicles" in Whelford, a village which lies directly east of the base, by a member of the public in the early hours of Sunday morning.

The woman who called 999 told the BBC it was "pure luck" she had spotted them, having arrived home to find the road blocked and a "large group of hooded and masked men".

"I believe that my 999 call foiled whatever plans they had," she said.

A bomb disposal team arrived on scene shortly afterwards and a 400m (1,312ft) cordon was put in place.

But Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, told reporters on Tuesday that the police response that morning was due to "a range of information".

Police cordons near the base are expected to be completely lifted on Wednesday, while residents from the 85 homes evacuated on Sunday have been allowed to return to their properties.

The five men are all UK nationals aged between 23 and 25. Four of them live in Westminster and one in Camden, and searches of their homes are now complete.

Assistant Commissioner Taylor previously said their bail was "subject to stringent conditions on their movement and contact with others" as they remained under investigation.

"The safety of the public is at the forefront of our investigative decision-making, and this was certainly the case yesterday," he said on Tuesday.

"I understand why this development was surprising to some, but I would like to reiterate that this is an investigative decision and one which is grounded in experience and strategy."

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday told journalists he was "disappointed" the five men had been released on bail.

Asked whether this had been a "long-standing investigation", he said: "Yeah."

The RAF base has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force (USAF) for decades.

In recent months, US bombers have taken off from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.

In July, Iran said "any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces".

Assistant Commissioner Taylor has said officers are exploring "multiple lines of inquiry", including whether proxies or individuals knowingly or unknowingly working on behalf of a foreign state were involved.

In an update on Tuesday, he added that the incident had been worrying for many people, with this "heightened by the international commentary that we are seeing" in an apparent reference to comments from the US administration.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham chaired a Cobra meeting on Monday afternoon and urged people "not to speculate while the authorities establish the full facts".

The Iranian embassy in London said that it "categorically rejects and strongly condemns" what it called "unfounded and malicious speculations" linking Iran to the incident.

articles.title: Man found dead on tracks at Brooklyn subway station after his bag reportedly gets stuck in closing doors
articles.summary: Yaw Boahene's shopping bag reportedly got caught in closing subway doors at a Brooklyn station, dragging the 57-year-old onto the tracks of a northbound A train.
articles.body: A 57-year-old man was killed in Brooklyn Monday evening after his bag reportedly became trapped in closing subway doors, dragging him beneath the train. After a 911 call, Yaw Boahene was found "unconscious and unresponsive" on the tracks of a northbound A train at the Utica Avenue station in Brooklyn's Bedford-Stuyvesant neighborhood shortly after 6 p.m., according to the New York Police Department. Responding paramedics pronounced Boahene dead, and an investigation has been launched into the cause of his death. NYC SUSPECT FREED FROM PSYCH HOLD HOURS BEFORE FATAL SUBWAY SHOVING OF 76-YEAR-OLD FORMER TEACHER Boahene, of Brooklyn, was exiting a train at around 6 p.m. when his shopping bag got stuck in the doors, The New York Times reported. Incidents involving commuters being caught and dragged by subway trains are exceedingly rare, but they do happen. In October 2022, Joseph Ancona, 20, was killed in the Columbus Circle station when his bag was caught in a door, dragging him onto the tracks before he was fatally struck by the train, FOX 5 New York reported at the time.
